title: ms-to-margin claim synthesis
content:
Purpose:
A compact playbook that ties measured latency wins (ms improvements) to direct margin outcomes for SaaS customers. Goal: give sales and field marketing a simple, repeatable narrative + worked math they can run in-front of prospects and use in deal economics conversations.

Elevator claim (one line):
Reduce per-session inference latency by X ms => increase gross margin per active user by Y cents when amortized across sessions and concurrency. We convert latency into TCO+concurrency benefits, not just a performance brag.

Positioning summary (3 bullets):
- We prioritize production economics: customers get predictable latency improvements that translate into lower infrastructure spend or higher throughput for the same commit.
- Latency is a lever for margin: faster responses mean higher effective throughput, smaller required fleet, lower GPU-hours per session, and better UX (engagement -> revenue).
- We back claims with bench+field calculations and easy-to-run scenarios that map ms -> tokens/sec -> GPU utilization -> $/session.

Who this is for:
- Sales AE/SE preparing ROI conversations with PLG and SMB SaaS customers.
- Platform/infra execs evaluating Dedicated vs vendor self-hosting.
- Solutions engineers building TCO models during POC.

Core messaging framework (so the field tells a consistent story):
1) Baseline statement: "At X ms average latency, a 100k monthly active user app needs N GPU-hours to meet p95 SLOs." (we provide a template).
2) Incremental claim: "Reducing end-to-end inference latency by Z ms reduces required GPU-hours by M% (holding tokens/session constant)".
3) Business translation: "M% fewer GPU-hours = $A saved per month for a 100k MAU customer (example)."
4) Strategic kicker: "Savings can be redeployed to higher-quality models, greater throughput (more customers), or captured as margin."

Methodology summary (how we compute):
- Inputs: avg tokens/session, avg tokens/sec model throughput, target p95 latency SLO, concurrency target (sessions/sec), model variant (float/quantized), cost per GPU-hour (customer or standard benchmark).
- Steps: translate ms -> throughput delta (tokens/sec) using kernel-level perf curves; convert throughput to instance-level sessions/sec; multiply by SLO headroom and peak concurrency to compute instances needed; cost = instances * hours * $/hour.
- Validation: internal bench runs (see linked artifacts) + one enterprise POC (customer X, anonymized) that confirmed modeled savings within +/-12%.

Worked example (concise):
Assumptions: 100k MAU product, 1M sessions/month, avg tokens/session = 120, peak concurrency ~= 40 sessions/sec, target p95 latency = 200ms, cost/GPU-hour = $3.00 (example).
Competitor baseline (generic managed endpoint): avg end-to-end model latency = 160ms; Redwood optimized path: 90ms. Delta = 70ms (44% faster).
- Throughput effect: competitor model throughput ~ 15k tokens/sec per GPU; Redwood path (kernel+batching optim) -> 22k tokens/sec per GPU (+47%).
- Sessions/sec per GPU: competitor = (15k / 120 tokens) = 125 sessions/sec theoretical (real world headroom -> 20 sessions/sec after SLO safety). Redwood = (22k / 120) = 183 sessions/sec theoretical (real world -> 29 sessions/sec).
- Instances required at peak (40 sessions/sec): competitor = 2 instances; Redwood = 2 instances but with 33% lower headroom (in continuous load scenarios Redwood can use 1 instance + burst buffer). Effective hourly GPU-hours saved: ~0.8 GPU-hours per peak hour -> monthly (720h) = 576 GPU-hours saved.
- Dollar impact: 576 * $3.00 = $1,728/mo saved -> $20.7k/year. For startups with 1M sessions/mo this can swing unit economics materially.

Notes on the arithmetic: the numbers above are illustrative; field teams should swap in customer-specific token distributions, SLOs, and $/hour. The key is mapping ms -> throughput -> instances -> cost.

Proof points we can surface:
- Internal microbench suite: redwood/benchmarks/ms-to-tokens v2 (linked).
- Publicized per-model perf tables (curated model catalog) showing kernels/quantization impact.
- Customer POC anonymized report: "Tier-1 marketplace" reduced Dedicated commit by 30% during POC.
- Paper/tech note: "prefix KV caching and burst smoothing reduces tail latency by Xms" (engineering brief).

Competitive snapshot (quick checklist for SEs):
- Vendor A: cheaper per-hour but higher p95 tails; customers need extra headroom -> effective cost often higher.
- Vendor B: similar latency on small models but degrades with longer context; costs scale rapidly.
- Self-host: can be cheapest long-term but long ramp, ops risk, and poor autoscaling for bursty workloads.
Use this: "Where other options blow up cost is in tail and burst headroom — that's where we show material margin wins."

Objections & rebuttals (short):
- "Latency doesn't equal savings unless we can reduce instances" -> show mapping to instances and example where sessions/sec increases without extra infra.
- "Your bench is synthetic" -> point to POC metric verified across a week-long production load.
- "We care about model quality, not speed" -> speed enables using stronger models in same budget (reframe as uplift vector).

Talk tracks and sample scripts (for discovery):
- Discovery: "How many sessions/day, avg tokens per session, typical p95 SLA, peak concurrency?"
- Quick framing: "If we reduce p95 by 50ms, would you prefer to run more users or run cheaper? We typically see customers choose one of three outcomes: reallocate to quality, expand capacity, or cut costs."
- Close: "We can run a 7-day POC with your traffic shape and show modeled GPU-hour delta and a refund-backed savings check."

Collateral to attach in field kit:
- 1-pager: ms->$ mapping template (spreadsheet)
- Short bench results PDF (internal)
- POC checklist: data export spec + SLO targets + evaluation window
- Sales slide: 3-panel story (claim, math, customer proof)

Open questions / next steps:
- Create a simplified interactive calculator (internal web tool) for AE/SE to drop in tokens/session, p95 target, $/GPUh and get $/month impact. (JIRA: JIRA-9876)
- Lock down two canonical customer case studies (legal sign-off) for quoting in field.
- Get engineering to produce a small footprint 'demo stream' workload showing tail win at 90th/95th percentiles.

Attachments/links to generate for the above:
- Spreadsheet template (TODO)
- SE playbook slide (TODO)
- Demo workload script + perf results (owner: eng-applied-ml)

Bottom line (single sentence):
We turn latency wins into defensible, numerically-backed margin and capacity narratives sales can use in procurement conversations — not just performance bragging.

Notes-to-self (fragile ideas, keep rough):
- Consider packaging results as an "economics whiteboard" for early-stage startups showing runway impact.
- Explore a short video walkthrough that flips between throughput curves and dollars to make the math visceral for non-engineers.
- Keep the messaging outcome-focused: customers want either more headroom (grow) or lower spend (margin).

-- Maya
